identity.title: The multi-thermal chromosphere. Inversions of ALMA and IRIS data

paper_type_evidence.quote: We use the STiC nonlocal thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) inversion code to simultaneously fit real ultraviolet and mm spectra in order to infer the thermodynamic parameters of the plasma.

evidence.quote: ALMA and IRIS co-observed part of a plage on the eastern side of the active region NOAA 12651 at $\mu\approx0.92$
ALMA and IRIS co-observed part of a plage on the eastern side of the active region NOAA 12651 at $\mu\approx0.92$

question.value: How do temperature and microturbulence stratification in plage and quiet Sun change when ALMA 1.25 mm continuum is added to NLTE inversions of IRIS NUV spectra, and what do cool holes and hot transient brightenings imply?

evidence.quote: We revisit the problem of the stratification of temperature and microturbulence in plage and the quiet Sun, now adding millimeter (mm) continuum observations provided by the Atacama Large Millimiter Array (ALMA)
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00050.S.
resulting in one brightness temperature map at 2 s cadence corresponding to the central frequency of Band 6 and thus to an effective wavelength of 1.25 mm
Along with the Mg II h and k lines we fit two of the UV triplet lines

evidence.quote: consist of five interferometric scans (cite: 2017SoPh..292...87S) and five single-dish scans of the full solar disk with Total Power (TP) antennas
maximum ALMA resolution ($\sim$0.8")
The noise level is $\sim30$ K at most.

analysis_steps.goal: Reduce and align ALMA and IRIS data

method.value: Process ALMA with SoAP2, rescale TP to 5900 K, combine up to 14 ALMA images per IRIS raster, interpolate to common grid, convert Tb to intensity via Planck function

evidence.quote: Up to 14 ALMA images were then combined to replicate the IRIS rasters

analysis_steps.goal: NLTE inversions of IRIS vs IRIS+ALMA

method.value: STiC regularized Levenberg-Marquardt inversion of Mg II h&k, UV triplet, Ni I, NUV continuum with and without the 1.25 mm point; NLTE hydrogen ionization, free-free mm opacity

evidence.quote: which is a regularized Levenberg-Marquardt code for multi-atom NLTE inversions of multiple spectral lines and continua including partial frequency redistribution (PRD) effects

key_parameters.value: 19 temperature nodes, 9 vturb nodes, 7 vLOS nodes

evidence.quote: We used nine and seven equidistant nodes for $v_{\rm turb}$ and $v_{\rm LOS}$, respectively.

key_parameters.value: IRIS instrumental profile Gaussian FWHM 53 mÅ

evidence.quote: Gaussian function with a fullwidth at half maximum of 53 mÅ

assumptions.value: 1D plane-parallel hydrostatic atmosphere; instantaneous NLTE electron densities; cyclotron and synchrotron neglected

evidence.quote: STiC code which assumes a 1D, plane-parallel atmosphere in hydrostatic equilibrium

fitting.value: chi2 minimization with regularization penalties and ad hoc ALMA weighting

evidence.quote: we introduced an *ad hoc* weighting function that ensures that the ALMA data are well fitted

validation.value: Monte Carlo tests for overfitting; node-count tests

evidence.quote: we ran a set of Monte Carlo simulations as explained in Section

method.value: Numerical temperature response functions; up to 100 Monte Carlo inversions per pixel with random starting atmospheres

evidence.quote: we ran sets of up to $n=100$ Monte Carlo simulations per pixel of synthetic IRIS and ALMA data generated from the best-fit models
accurate (to <0.5%) 68% confidence intervals on the parameters

analysis_steps.goal: Synthesize CO lines in cool holes

method.value: LTE vibration-rotation CO lines near 4.67 micron computed from inverted models

evidence.quote: We computed a few vibration-rotation CO lines in the commonly observed near-infrared (NIR) range around 4.67 $\rm \mu m$ assuming LTE.

method.value: Invert 18 time steps (~7.5 min) with IRIS and IRIS+ALMA; compare temperature, vturb, vLOS and Mg II wavelength-time diagrams

evidence.loc: 4.5 Time evolution of the plage region
evidence.quote: We inverted 18 time steps, which is about $\sim7.5$ min (before ALMA pauses for calibration)
The inversions were performed with the STockholm Inversion Code
as implemented in CASA
using version four of the calibration files obtained using the *iris_get_response* routine in SolarSoft
This research has made use of SunPy, an open-source and free community-developed solar data analysis Python package

findings_qualitative.value: IRIS-only inversions fail to reproduce observed ALMA contrast; adding ALMA increases temperature contrast and lowers microturbulence

evidence.quote: the IRIS+ALMA inversions have increased contrast and temperature range, and tend to favor lower values of microturbulence

claims.hypothesis: Does mm continuum constrain chromospheric temperature and microturbulence in NLTE inversions of real data?
claims.experiment: Compare IRIS-only and IRIS+ALMA STiC inversions
claims.result: IRIS+ALMA gives higher temperature contrast and lower vturb (median ~2 vs ~4 km/s)
claims.finding: ALMA provides a useful constraint on chromospheric temperature and vturb

evidence.quote: We confirm the anticipated constraining potential of ALMA in NLTE inversions of the solar chromosphere.

claims.hypothesis: Cool ALMA holes are chromospheric and could host CO
claims.experiment: Inversions with more nodes plus LTE CO synthesis
claims.result: Temperature dips at logtau -6 to -5 reproduce cool mm values; CO lines show small chromospheric contribution
claims.finding: Localized cool regions may allow CO to form

evidence.quote: the inversions require the existence of localized low-temperature regions in the chromosphere where molecules such as CO could form.

claims.hypothesis: Hot mm brightenings relate to shocks and non-equilibrium ionization
claims.experiment: Time series inversions and Mg II wavelength-time diagrams
claims.result: ~2000 K temperature rise, velocity gradient sign change, 3.5-4 min Mg II shock pattern
claims.finding: Shock heating, possibly with non-equilibrium hydrogen ionization

evidence.quote: The hot features could sustain such high temperatures due to non-equilibrium hydrogen ionization effects in a shocked chromosphere

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: LTE hydrogen ionization rejected in favour of NLTE electron densities, which are more uniform and more realistic

evidence.quote: We compared inversions with LTE and NLTE hydrogen ionization and verified that the NLTE calculations give us much more uniform electron densities

limitations_admitted.value: STiC cannot treat time-dependent hydrogen ionization; 1D plane-parallel assumption; resolution difference between IRIS and ALMA

evidence.quote: It is not possible to take these effects into account with STiC or with any other current inversion code to our knowledge.

referee_caveats_inferred: Ad hoc ALMA weighting may force fits and bias results
Single field and single raster/short time series limits generality
Absolute ALMA Tb scale uncertain by up to 10-15%
Cool holes fit poorly, so CO inference rests on imperfect models
